title: Crash in [@ mozilla::dom::syncedcontext::Transaction<T>::Commit] with CanSet failed for field(s): OpenerPolicy
body:
Crash report: https://crash-stats.mozilla.org/report/index/001e9464-e793-4c9c-a96a-3148b0230317

MOZ_CRASH Reason: ```CanSet failed for field(s): OpenerPolicy```

Top 10 frames of crashing thread:
```
0  libxul.so  MOZ_Crash  mfbt/Assertions.h:261
0  libxul.so  mozilla::dom::syncedcontext::Transaction<mozilla::dom::BrowsingContext>::Commit  docshell/base/SyncedContextInlines.h:103
1  libxul.so  mozilla::dom::BrowsingContext::SetOpenerPolicy  docshell/base/BrowsingContext.h:277
2  libxul.so  mozilla::dom::Document::StartDocumentLoad  dom/base/Document.cpp:3539
3  libxul.so  nsHTMLDocument::StartDocumentLoad  dom/html/nsHTMLDocument.cpp:350
4  libxul.so  nsContentDLF::CreateDocument  layout/build/nsContentDLF.cpp:315
5  libxul.so  nsContentDLF::CreateInstance  layout/build/nsContentDLF.cpp
6  libxul.so  nsDocShell::NewContentViewerObj  docshell/base/nsDocShell.cpp:8109
6  libxul.so  nsDocShell::CreateContentViewer  docshell/base/nsDocShell.cpp:7843
6  libxul.so  nsDSURIContentListener::DoContent  docshell/base/nsDSURIContentListener.cpp:168
```

This particular field appears to be the most popular current cause of this crash signature. It looks like it is mostly Fenix for whatever reason.

There are some bugs on file for this signature, but not for this specific field as far as I can see.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
One thing that I noted was that before Fenix version 106.1.0 we didn't hit this assert, but instead we hit [this](https://crash-stats.mozilla.org/report/index/ba5ee597-58ca-4cf7-b686-a8af60230418) crash, which in turn got fixed by bug 1790203. The question is: are we seeing a similar root cause and what implications does it have to have the call to [`WindowContext::SetEmbedderPolicy`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/dom/base/Document.cpp#6872-6876) be delayed, possible to after the call to [`BrowsingContext::SetOpenerPolicy`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/dom/base/Document.cpp#3530). `EmbedderPolicy` isn't directly translated to `OpenerPolicy` but it is used in a [couple of places](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/search?q=WindowContext%3A%3AGetEmbedderPolicy&path=&case=false&regexp=false)

Emilio and Sean might know more, but I'll contiue digging.

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
So the line crashing is [this one](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5c922d8b93b43c18bf65539bfc72a30f84989003/dom/base/Document.cpp#3530) right?

I don't think it's quite the same root cause. `BrowsingContext::CanSet` for `OpenerPolicy` is about the exact values that get set. That other bug was about an origin trial, where we try to process the trial before the window context is initialized. This code runs unconditionally right?

But, I think [this code](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5c922d8b93b43c18bf65539bfc72a30f84989003/netwerk/protocol/http/HttpBaseChannel.cpp#5967-5975) and the origin trial might still be involved to some extent. In particular, it seems feasible that:

 * Document A gets served with `Origin-trial: <valid-token>`, ends up being cross-origin isolated.
 * Document B doesn't, and we try to set the opener policy and fail.

Questions I have:

 * Why is it ok to set something global to the browsing-context based on the document's channel?
 * What is supposed to guarantee the invariant that CanSet is effectively asserting? Should the caller check instead?

I'm not familiar enough with COEP (I only reviewed the origin-trial bits) to know the answers to those off-hand.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
Yep, that line.

In a Windows crash I can see the policy being set is `OPENER_POLICY_UNSAFE_NONE`, which means that the `OpenerPolicy` of the `BrowsingContext` is `OPENER_POLICY_SAME_ORIGIN_EMBEDDER_POLICY_REQUIRE_CORP` and we're effectively trying to downgrade it.

This points to [`HttpBaseChannel::mComputedCrossOriginOpenerPolicy`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/netwerk/protocol/http/HttpBaseChannel.h#776) either not being set at all, or not being set in time. 

If we look at how `BrowsingContext` is [created](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/docshell/base/BrowsingContext.cpp#388-413), a `BrowsingContext` can be initialized with `OPENER_POLICY_SAME_ORIGIN_EMBEDDER_POLICY_REQUIRE_CORP` that it inherits from an opener. For this case, we know that the crash happens in a top level content browsing context, so _if_ we're seeing that Document A gets an origin trial token and becomes cross-origin isolated, then opens Document B to the same site, but not serving it then this should be fairly trivial to write a test for.

But _if_ this is what we're seeing, my bet would be that we'd see it on all platforms equally prevalent, but Android dominates. And Android doesn't run Fission, which also is something that might be interfering here.

I'll continue digging. I'll clear Sean's ni, and ask Valentin if he has any ideas to what might be happening. Because I don't think that it's necessarily setting the opener policy and crashing that's the problem, but that we're actually setting it to something bad.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
I think the DocumentChannel works a bit differently on Android, but I don't really know how.

I would have expected the COOP policy to be computed by the time we call the listener, but looking at the stack trace from the crash it seems the request is coming from a JAR channel instead?
18 	libxul.so 	nsJARChannel::OnStartRequest(nsIRequest*) 	modules/libjar/nsJARChannel.cpp:1230 	cfi

So I'm not totally sure what the JS code in the middle is doing, or what channel is being passed to `nsDocumentOpenInfo::OnStartRequest(nsIRequest*)`

Maybe Nika has a better idea of what's happening there.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body: Latest clue is how error pages are [handled on android](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/85b4f7363292b272eb9b606e00de2c37a6be73f0/docshell/base/nsDocShell.cpp#3792-3809). I guess what could happen is that we try to load an error page in a document with `OPENER_POLICY_SAME_ORIGIN_EMBEDDER_POLICY_REQUIRE_CORP`, but the error page has a channel that isn't set up for that. Does that sound plausible :participant8?

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
I discussed this a bit with :farre over matrix, and noticed that there's some JS on the stack between the callback from a JAR channel (as noted in comment 11) and the actual callback which is apparently seeing a HTTP(s) channel. This suggests that we're probably actually loading a PDF through the PDF.js stream converter. This handles the `onStartRequest` from the original HTTP(s) channel, and instead sends the data from a local resource (the PDF.js viewer: https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/85b4f7363292b272eb9b606e00de2c37a6be73f0/toolkit/components/pdfjs/content/PdfStreamConverter.sys.mjs#19) instead, pretending like it's coming from the HTTP(s) channel: https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/85b4f7363292b272eb9b606e00de2c37a6be73f0/toolkit/components/pdfjs/content/PdfStreamConverter.sys.mjs#1138.

Theoretically this should be passing through the original HTTP(s) channel, but perhaps something else is going wrong under the hood here leading to the confusion. I'd look into seeing if we can reproduce this by serving a PDF with the `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` and `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` headers set, then try navigating to it.

I don't know if that'd reproduce the issue inherently, so there's also a chance that it needs to have slightly different header configurations in some way.

There's also a chance, I suppose, that this requires `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: credentialless` which I think is behind origin-trial right now (https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/85b4f7363292b272eb9b606e00de2c37a6be73f0/netwerk/protocol/http/HttpBaseChannel.cpp#5946-5964), or that it requires some special situations around e.g. service workers and interception - but starting simple seems better for now.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
Created attachment 9333106
Bug 1823817 - Process cross origin security headers from nsHttpChannel::OnAuthCancelled.


nsHttpChannel::OnAuthCancelled calls nsHttpChannel::CallOnStartRequest
directly, effectively bypassing
HttpBaseChannel::ProcessCrossOriginSecurityHeaders, which is needed to
get CORP handling right.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
I've found something that I know is wrong, but I'm not entirely sure how to fix. the trouble is in nsHttpChannel::OnAuthCancelled. The docs say that it needs to call OnStartRequest, but it calls CallOnStartRequest. My problem is that this bypasses ProcessCrossOriginSecurityHeaders, which makes us crash, eventually, at https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/dom/base/Document.cpp#3530.

That crash is correct, because we're loading an error page that doesn't have the correct security headers for the site we canceled the auth prompt for.  What's missing is to somehow have nsHttpChannel::OnAuthCancelled call ProcessCrossOriginSecurityHeaders before calling CallOnStartRequest, but I'm not sure if it's that easy.

I've attached a patch that does exactly that, and I'm also moving it to Networking where the bug actually is.
